title: Conjecture 1 (Elphick, Farber, Goldberg, Wocjan)
statement_text: For every connected graph $G$ of order $n$, $s(G) \geq n - 1$.
context_text: Here $s(G) = \min\{s^+(G), s^-(G)\}$ is the square energy of $G$, where $s^+(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i^2$ and $s^-(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i < 0} \lambda_i^2$. The conjecture was motivated by the equality $s(G) = |\mathcal{E}(G)|$ for every bipartite graph. It has been verified for several graph classes including regular graphs, but the general case is wide open; the best known general lower bound prior to this paper was $\sqrt{n}$.
paper_contribution: Proves the first known linear lower bound $s(G) \geq \frac{3n}{4}$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n \geq 4$, via a superadditivity result for positive and negative square energies over vertex-induced subgraphs.
paper_title: A Linear Lower Bound for the Square Energy of Graphs

title: Informal Conjecture (improved linear bound)
statement_text: We believe the bound $s(G)\ge\frac{3n}{4}$ for every connected graph $G$ of order $n\ge4$ can be improved to $\frac{4n}{5}$ using more intricate partitioning of the graph $G$ and applying the superadditivity of $s^+$ and $s^-$ over vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs.
context_text: Graphs are simple. Let $\lambda_1\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$. The positive and negative square energies are $s^+(G)=\sum_{\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i^2$ and $s^-(G)=\sum_{\lambda_i<0}\lambda_i^2$, and the square energy is $s(G)=\min\{s^+(G),s^-(G)\}$. Since $s(G)=|E(G)|$ for bipartite graphs, Elphick, Farber, Goldberg and Wocjan conjectured that every connected graph of order $n$ satisfies $s(G)\ge n-1$; it is known for several classes including regular graphs, and the best previous general bound was $\sqrt n$. The authors prove that if $H_1,\dots,H_k$ are vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs of $G$ then $s^+(G)\ge\sum_i s^+(H_i)$ and $s^-(G)\ge\sum_i s^-(H_i)$, and deduce, by partitioning a connected graph into connected pieces, the first linear bound $s(G)\ge\frac{3n}{4}$ for connected $G$ of order $n\ge4$. They believe $\frac{4n}{5}$ is reachable with a more intricate partition, but did not do it because they believe more ideas are needed to reach $n-1$.
notes: PDF source — fractions are garbled by extraction; '4n − 5' and '3n − 4' in the raw text are interpreted as $\frac{4n}{5}$ and $\frac{3n}{4}$ respectively, consistent with the paper's proved result and the surrounding context.
paper_title: A Linear Lower Bound for the Square Energy of Graphs
